AFK.plain: You start the AI working, then walk away and let it run on its own.

AGENTS.md.plain: A readme file for the AI: instructions it reads at the start of every session.

AI.plain: A label for whatever computers can newly do that seems smart. Today that mostly means chatbots built on large language models.

AX.plain: How easy your project makes life for an AI agent, like developer experience but for the AI.

Agent mode.plain: A preset that sets how freely the AI may act and how it should behave. It can be switched mid-session.

Agent.plain: An AI model plus tools and instructions, working through a task with you turn by turn.

Attention budget.plain: The AI can only give so much focus to everything it reads, and that amount doesn't grow when the text gets longer.

Attention degradation.plain: The longer the conversation gets, the thinner the AI's focus is spread, so it misses more.

Attention relationship.plain: How strongly two pieces of text influence each other when the AI reads them.

Autocompact.plain: The tool automatically summarises the conversation when it is nearly full.

Automated check.plain: Tests, type checks and linters that pass or fail on their own, with no judgement involved.

Automated review.plain: A second AI reads the first AI's work and gives its opinion.

Cache tokens.plain: Text the provider remembers from your last request, so resending it costs much less.

Clearing.plain: Wipe the conversation and start again with a blank slate.

Compaction.plain: Summarise the conversation so far and carry the summary into a fresh one. You lose some detail to free up space.

Context pointer.plain: A note that tells the AI where to find more information, so it only reads it when needed.

Context window.plain: Everything the AI can see at once. It has a fixed size.

Context.plain: The information the AI has in front of it that matters for the task right now.

Contextual knowledge.plain: Facts the AI can read directly in the conversation, as opposed to what it learned in training.

DX.plain: How easy a codebase and its tools make good work for human developers.

Dark factory.plain: Code written by automated agents that no human ever reviews.

Design concept.plain: The shared idea of what you are building that you and the AI both hold in your heads.

Effort.plain: A dial for how long the AI thinks before answering. More thinking helps with hard problems but costs more.

Environment.plain: Everything the agent works on and can change: your files, tools and systems.

Filesystem.plain: The folders and files the agent can read, write and run.

Grilling.plain: The AI asks you questions one at a time until a plan is clear.

Hallucination.plain: The AI states something wrong with confidence: an invented fact, or ignoring what you gave it.

Handoff artifact.plain: A document written by one session so the next one can pick up the work.

Handoff.plain: Passing work from one AI session to another, with no going back.

Harness.plain: The software around the model (tools, instructions, permissions) that turns it into an agent.

Human review.plain: A person reads the code the AI wrote and judges it.

Human-in-the-loop.plain: A person works alongside the AI during the session, checking and steering as it goes.

Inference.plain: The AI generating an answer from what it already learned. It doesn't learn anything new while doing so.

Input tokens.plain: The text you send to the AI with each request. It costs less than the text the AI writes back.

Knowledge cutoff.plain: The date after which the AI learned nothing, so newer tools and libraries may be unknown to it.

MCP.plain: A standard way to plug extra tools and data sources into an AI app.

Memory system.plain: A way to save notes between sessions so the AI can recall them next time.

Model provider request.plain: One message from your tool to the AI company, and the answer coming back.

Model provider.plain: The company or software that runs the AI model for you.

Model.plain: The trained AI itself. It predicts text and does nothing else on its own.

Next-token prediction.plain: What the AI actually does: pick the next small chunk of text, then repeat.

Non-determinism.plain: Ask the same question twice and you may get different answers.

Output tokens.plain: The text the AI writes back. It costs more than the text you send.

Parameters.plain: The billions of numbers inside a model that hold everything it learned.

Parametric knowledge.plain: What the AI learned in training and stored in its parameters. It stops at training time.

Permission mode.plain: The setting that decides which actions the AI can take without asking you.

Permission request.plain: The prompt that asks you to approve something before the AI does it.

Prefix cache.plain: The provider reuses its work on the start of a request that hasn't changed, which saves time and money.

Primary source.plain: The original thing itself: the code, the transcript, the raw data.

Progressive disclosure.plain: Give the AI only what it needs now, with pointers to the rest.

Prototyping.plain: Ask the AI for a quick rough version so you have something real to react to.

Sandbox.plain: A walled-off space where the AI can run without harming the rest of your computer.

Secondary source.plain: A summary or account of the original: quick to read but missing detail.

Session.plain: One run of work with an AI, from a blank start until you clear or close it.

Skill.plain: A packaged set of instructions the AI loads only when a task calls for it.

Smart zone.plain: Early in a session the AI is sharp. As the session fills up it gets sloppier and more forgetful.

Software factory.plain: A setup where triggers, not people, start AI sessions so more work runs on its own.

Spec.plain: A written description of a larger piece of work, split into tickets for several sessions.

Stateless.plain: Remembers nothing between requests unless you send it again.

Subagent.plain: A helper agent that another agent starts for a side task and that reports back with a single answer.

Sycophancy.plain: The AI agrees with you too readily, because training rewarded answers people liked.

System prompt.plain: The standing instructions sent to the AI at the start of every request.

Ticket.plain: A single task written up for one session, possibly part of a larger spec.

Token.plain: A small chunk of text, roughly a word, that the AI reads and writes. Costs and limits are counted in tokens.

Tool call.plain: The AI asking, in plain text, to use a tool. The software around it does the actual running.

Tool result.plain: What comes back after a tool runs: file contents, output or an error.

Tool.plain: An action the agent can take, like reading a file or running a command.

Training.plain: Teaching the model by showing it huge amounts of text until it predicts well.

Turn.plain: One message from you plus everything the AI does before it hands control back.

Vibe coding.plain: Accepting the AI's code without reading it.
